newsitem.title: UK: Sears board considers shake-up, analysts say.
newsitem.headline: Sears board considers shake-up, analysts say.

text.p: A major shake-up of British retailer Sears Plc could be imminent as the group's embattled chief executive Liam Strong was due to put restructuring plans to the board on Thursday, including rationalisation of loss-making British Shoe Corporation, retail analysts said.
They said this was Strong's last chance to try and restore value to Sears' shares, which have been underperforming and were languishing near historic lows at around 79 pence on Thursday.
Industry sources said the board meeting would also consider Sears' plans to sell its Freemans home shopping arm to Littlewoods.
British press reports have suggested Strong would reshape the group into two divisions, Selfridges the department store and womenswear, and would shed BSC at a cost of 50 million stg.
There has been persistent speculation about a break-up of the entire group, including a spin off of Selfridges, valued at some 550 million stg.
Sears had no comment other than to say the board would meet ahead of the group's annual results, due to be published next Tuesday.
